title: Citizenship Act, 1955 (Act No. 57 of 1955)

sections.title: Citizenship by birth
sections.text: Every person born in India— (a) on or after the 26th day of January, 1950, but before the 1st day of July, 1987; (b) on or after the 1st day of July, 1987, but before the commencement of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 and either of whose parents is a citizen of India at the time of his birth; (c) on or after the commencement of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003, where both parents are citizens or one parent is a citizen and the other is not an illegal migrant, shall be a citizen of India by birth.

sections.title: Citizenship by registration
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of this section and such other conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed, the Central Government may, on an application made in this behalf, register as a citizen of India any person who is not an illegal migrant if he belongs to any of the specified categories.

sections.title: Special provisions as to citizenship of persons covered by the Assam Accord
sections.text: All persons of Indian origin who came before the 1st day of January, 1966 to Assam from Bangladesh and have been ordinarily resident in Assam since shall be deemed to be citizens of India as from the 1st day of January, 1966.

sections.title: Termination of citizenship
sections.text: Any citizen of India who by naturalisation, registration or otherwise voluntarily acquires, or has at any time between the 26th January, 1950 and the commencement of this Act voluntarily acquired the citizenship of another country shall, upon such acquisition, cease to be a citizen of India.

summary: Governs the acquisition, renunciation, termination, and deprivation of Indian citizenship enacted by Parliament pursuant to Article 11 of the Constitution.
text: Citizenship Act, 1955 (Act No. 57 of 1955). Enacted under Article 11 of the Constitution of India. Regulates citizenship by birth (Section 3), descent (Section 4), registration (Section 5), naturalisation (Section 6), special provisions for Assam Accord (Section 6A), and termination of citizenship (Section 9).

title: Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Act No. 43 of 1951)

sections.title: Disqualification on conviction for certain offences
sections.text: A person convicted of any offence punishable under certain specified sections of the Indian Penal Code or special statutes, or convicted of any other offence and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than two years, shall be disqualified from the date of conviction and shall continue to be disqualified for a further period of six years since release. In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), subsection (4) providing 3-month protection pending appeal was struck down by the Supreme Court as unconstitutional under Article 102(1)(e).

sections.title: Registration with the Election Commission of associations and bodies as political parties
sections.text: Any association or body of individual citizens of India calling itself a political party and intending to avail itself of the provisions of this Part shall make an application to the Election Commission for its registration as a political party, pledging true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established.

sections.title: Corrupt practices
sections.text: The following shall be deemed to be corrupt practices for the purposes of this Act: (1) Bribery; (2) Undue influence; (3) The appeal by a candidate or his agent to vote or refrain from voting on the ground of religion, race, caste, community or language (as interpreted by 7-judge Constitution Bench in Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen, 2017); (4) Publication of false statements in relation to personal character.

summary: Primary statute governing the conduct of elections to the Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures, qualifications and disqualifications of members, corrupt practices, and election disputes under Part XV of the Constitution.
text: Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Act No. 43 of 1951). Operates pursuant to Article 327 of the Constitution of India. Establishes administrative machinery for elections, qualifications and disqualifications under Section 8 (Lily Thomas), political party registration under Section 29A, and corrupt practices under Section 123.

title: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (Act No. 10 of 1994)
part_reference: Part III - Fundamental Rights & Part IV - DPSPs

sections.title: Definition of Human Rights
sections.text: 'Human rights' means the rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in the International Covenants and enforceable by courts in India.

sections.title: Constitution of a National Human Rights Commission
sections.text: The Central Government shall constitute a body to be known as the National Human Rights Commission to exercise the powers conferred upon, and to perform the functions assigned to, it under this Act, headed by a Chairperson who has been a Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court.

sections.title: Functions of the Commission
sections.text: The Commission shall inquire into complaints of violation of human rights or abetment thereof or negligence in the prevention of such violation by a public servant; intervene in court proceedings relating to human rights; visit jails and detention institutions; review constitutional and statutory safeguards.

summary: Establishes the National Human Rights Commission, State Human Rights Commissions, and Human Rights Courts for better protection of rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity under Article 21.
text: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (Act No. 10 of 1994). Translates Article 21 constitutional guarantees into institutional watchdog mechanisms: defines human rights under Section 2(1)(d), establishes NHRC under Section 3, and specifies investigatory functions under Section 12.

title: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act No. 22 of 2005)

sections.title: Right to information
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of this Act, all citizens shall have the right to information.

sections.title: Obligations of public authorities (Suo motu disclosure)
sections.text: Every public authority shall maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed and publish within one hundred and twenty days from the enactment of this Act particulars of its organization, functions, duties, decision-making procedure, norms, rules, regulations, and directory of officers.

sections.title: Exemption from disclosure of information
sections.text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, there shall be no obligation to give any citizen: (a) information disclosure of which would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India, security, strategic, scientific or economic interests of the State; (b) information forbidden by court; (c) parliamentary privilege; (d) commercial confidence or trade secrets; (e) fiduciary relationships unless larger public interest warrants; (j) personal information having no relationship to public activity.

summary: Operationalizes the Fundamental Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1)(a) by providing an effective statutory regime for citizens to secure access to information under control of public authorities.
text: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act No. 22 of 2005). Derived from Article 19(1)(a) as affirmed in State of UP v. Raj Narain (1975) and Bennett Coleman (1972). Codifies right to information under Section 3, proactive disclosure under Section 4, and public-interest exemptions under Section 8.

title: Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 (Act No. 28 of 1958)
part_reference: Part III - Fundamental Rights & Part XVIII - Emergency

sections.title: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas
sections.text: If the Governor of that State or the Administrator of that Union territory or the Central Government is of the opinion that the whole or any part of such State or Union territory is in such a disturbed or dangerous condition that the use of armed forces in aid of the civil power is necessary, they may declare the whole or such part to be a disturbed area.

sections.title: Special powers of the armed forces
sections.text: Any commissioned officer, warrant officer, non-commissioned officer or other person of equivalent rank in the armed forces may, in a disturbed area: (a) fire upon or use force, even to the causing of death, against any person acting in contravention of law or order prohibiting assembly of five or more persons; (b) destroy arms dumps or fortifications; (c) arrest without warrant; (d) enter and search premises without warrant.

sections.title: Protection to persons acting under Act (Sanction for prosecution)
sections.text: No prosecution, suit or other legal proceeding shall be instituted, except with the previous sanction of the Central Government, against any person in respect of anything done or purported to be done in exercise of the powers conferred by this Act.

summary: Grants special powers to armed forces in disturbed areas pursuant to Article 355 and Entry 2A of List I; upheld by Supreme Court Constitution Bench in Naga People's Movement of Human Rights v. Union of India (1998) subject to strict procedural safeguards and dos and don'ts.
text: Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 (Act No. 28 of 1958). Enacted under Article 355 and Entry 2A List I. Governs disturbed area declarations (Section 3), operational powers (Section 4), and requirement of central sanction for prosecution under Section 6.
